about: Key terms an examiner would expect a student to know from each document, marked from the text alone, before any system output was looked at. Written by an AI session on 23 Oct 2026: PROVISIONAL. Replace or confirm with two human raters (see docs/KEYTERMS.md). A term matches when it is the same words, ignoring case, plurals, hyphens and possessives.

documents.subject: Electrical engineering
documents.syllabus: Unit 1: DC Circuits - Ohm's law, resistance and conductance, series and parallel circuits, power and energy, Kirchhoff's laws (KCL, KVL), network analysis.

documents.subject: Engineering mathematics
documents.syllabus: Unit 2: Differential Calculus - limits and continuity, derivative of a function, rules of differentiation (power rule, product rule, quotient rule, chain rule), maxima and minima, stationary points, second derivative test.

documents.subject: Programming
documents.syllabus: Unit 4: Functions and Recursion - function calls and the call stack, recursion, base case, tail recursion, recursion vs iteration, recursive algorithms (factorial, binary search).

documents.subject: Systems programming
documents.syllabus: Unit 5: Linkers and Loaders - loader schemes (absolute loader, relocating loader, direct linking loader), relocation, linking, dynamic linking, overlays, address binding, design of a two-pass linker.

documents.subject: Information and cyber security
documents.syllabus: Unit III: Authentication and Key Management - secret key distribution, Diffie-Hellman key exchange, man-in-the-middle attack, hash functions, message digest, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, SHA-3, message authentication code (MAC), digital signatures.

documents.subject: Database management systems
documents.syllabus: Unit 4: Transactions and Concurrency - transaction concept, ACID properties, transaction states, concurrency control, lock-based protocols, two-phase locking, deadlock handling (prevention, detection, recovery), log-based recovery, write-ahead logging, checkpoints.

documents.subject: Distributed systems
documents.syllabus: Unit 1: Introduction - distributed computing, characteristics of distributed systems (resource sharing, concurrency, scalability, fault tolerance), message passing, remote procedure call (RPC), logical clocks, Lamport clocks, vector clocks.

documents.subject: Operating systems
documents.syllabus: Unit 3: Memory Management and Deadlocks - paging, page table, TLB, segmentation, fragmentation, deadlock conditions, deadlock avoidance (banker's algorithm), deadlock detection, CPU scheduling (FCFS, SJF, priority, round robin), starvation and aging.
